title: Standard progress note (F1) faithfulness (judge)
hypothesis: The default template is as faithful as SOAP.
notes: precision 96% (2/56); forbidden: none; e.g. The client's mood was subdued. | The client's affect was congruent with discussion of recent distress and sleep difficulties.

data.note:
Presentation
The client presented for a 50-minute individual CBT session diagnosed with F41.0 Panic disorder. The client was cooperative and engaged, reporting a rough week involving a panic attack at a grocery store. Mood was subdued, and affect was congruent with discussion of recent distress and sleep difficulties.

Session content
The client discussed experiencing a panic attack in a grocery store checkout line on Tuesday, reporting heart pounding and leaving the cart. The client identified catastrophic automatic thoughts: "That I was going to pass out in front of everyone and they would think I was crazy." The client completed two thought records out of the assigned three. Sleep was reported as poor, approximately four hours a night, with frequent awakenings around 3:00 AM. The client reported starting sertraline 50 mg approximately two weeks ago via their primary care physician, with initial nausea that has since resolved. The client also discussed frustration with unhelpful advice from their sister Dana regarding pushing through panic.

Interventions
Reviewed the client's completed thought records and examined belief ratings before and after panic events (CBT). Conducted an in-session interoceptive exposure exercise (spinning in a chair for 30 seconds to induce dizziness and observe physiological sensations) (CBT). Processed the client's response and anxiety levels during and after the exposure exercise (CBT). Discussed potential psychoeducation for family support, which the client deferred for the present (CBT).

Client response
The client responded positively to reviewing the thought record, recognizing a significant drop in belief regarding passing out from 90% in the moment down to 40% later at home. During the interoceptive exposure exercise, the client reported anxiety peaking at a 6 and observed that the physical sensations and anxiety decreased to a 3 within two minutes without fleeing, gaining insight that physiological sensations peak and pass on their own.

Risk assessment
No risk indicators were reported. The client denied thoughts of self-harm or not wanting to be alive, stating, "I just want the panic to stop."

Plan
Complete thought records three times this week. Practice the interoceptive spinning exercise once a day at home. Conduct a behavioral experiment by returning to the grocery store on a quiet Saturday morning and staying until anxiety drops by half. Schedule the next appointment for the same time next week.
